newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- F&C SAGA ENDS AS HYPO TAKES CONTROL OF TRUSTS

Foreign & Colonial investment trusts have reached agreement to sell control of their fund management company to Hypo-Bank of Germany for 60 million pounds stg. Five Foreign & Colonial trust will benefit from the cash payment while retaining a 35 percent stake in Hypo Foreign & Colonial Management through Pountney Hill, the holding company.
-- PAY-PER-VIEW SOCCER DEAL IS DENIED

The FA Premier League and BSkyB satellite broadcasting company put out statements last night denying that the two had agreed a pay-per-view match deal. The joint statement stated that there had been no talks between Sky Television and the clubs and that the Premier League is not involved in any talks on pay-per-view.
-- YORKSHIRE PULLS LOANS TWO HOURS AFTER LAUNCH

The Yorkshire Building Society withdrew a new range of capped, discounted and fixed rate mortgages after only two hours. The Society announced new mortgage rates at 11 am and then pulled the offer in the early afternoon, stating that the unexpected rise in inflation meant that swap prices on the money market were fluctuating so much. They had not bought the swaps needed to sustain the new rates before putting out the offer.
THE TIMES
-- CLARKE FACES CLASH OVER INFLATION LEAP

A large rise in inflation in October looks set to ignite a clash between the Chancellor and the Bank of England over interest rates. Headline inflation rose to 2.7 percent from 2.1 percent in September and the underlying rate hit 3.3 percent from 2.9 percent. The figures make the Government's target of 2.5 percent or less even less likely to be achieved. The underlying rate is now at its highest since September 1993.
-- BIG MAC POISED TO JOIN TEXACO WAR EFFORT

In an effort to gain market share in the UK petrol retailing market, Texaco has been in talks with McDonald's. The American oil company has plans to rapidly expand the number of petrol station sites that contain McDonald's restaurants and drive- through sales units.
-- AIRLINE LINK-UP FLIES INTO EU STORM

A formal investigation has been launched by the European Commission into the planned link-up between British Airways and American Airlines. Both airlines have been told in writing by the Commission that the proposed alliance does not appear to be in the interest of the consumer. They have 60 days to respond.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REBELS TRIUMPH AT GREYCOAT

Greycoat, the property group, was snubbed by its institutional investors yesterday as it attempted to defeat moves by rebel shareholders to push it into merger talks with Moorfield Estates, its smaller rival. At yesterday's extraordinary meeting, Greycoat had faced calls for its break up from Brian Myerson and Julian Teger, whose Active Value fund controls 11 percent of the company's shares. Instead of tabling his break-up motion, Mr Myerson called for an adjournment of the meeting, which would give Greycoat time to consider Moorfield's approach more carefully.
-- SCOTTISH WIDOWS TAKES A PROTECTOR

Scottish Widows, the mutual life insurer, announced yesterday it would be linking up with the Royal Bank of Scotland in a move to prevent a take over of the Black Widow. The deal could result in Scottish Widows buying around 20 percent of RBS's life insurance subsidiary, Royal Scottish Insurance.
-- NEW MEANS TO AID MOTORISTS

A new network of privatised regional traffic control centres could soon be giving motorists traffic information. The centres aim at relieving Britain's worsening road congestion are being considered by the Government in consultation with the Highways Agency. The plan is to harness the potential of the private sector and the centres will be located at key regional motorway centres.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BT ASKS GOVERNMENT TO LIFT GOLDEN SHARE

BT has started negotiations with the Government in the hope of removing its protection against takeovers provided since privatisation 12 years ago by the "golden share" in the company, which allows the Government to veto changes to BT's constitution. The move is aimed at convincing US regulators that the UK market is open to competition and get their approval of its proposed 13 billion pounds stg takeover of MCI, the American long-distance phone operator.
-- GUS SHARES SOAR ON 1 BILLION POUNDS ACQUISITION

The mail order giant, Great Universal Stores, agreed yesterday to pay 1 billion pounds stg for Experian, an American information services company. The surprise move is GUS's first significant acquisition in over 30 years. Shares in GUS rose 57.5p to 648p as the City took the news as the sign of a new era at the retail Giant.
-- 50 PERCENT FLOAT OF EQUITY & LAW COULD RAISE 400 MILLION POUNDS

Equity & Law is looking at a partial stock market flotation. The move could raise up to 400 million pounds stg. The partial flotation of up to 50 percent of Equity & Law's holding is thought to stem from initial discussions between the UK firm and its French parent, Axa, which announced a merger with French rival UAP group, earlier this week.
